en: How do you do, fair lady.
Indeed, I am not from these parts.
Nor am I. I was born in France.
But sadly, it seems we have different homes.
My name is Bridget.
A pleasure to make your acquaintance.
Out for a stroll? What a fine pastime.
Good morning. Are you going out?
How nice for men, free to live as you please.
We women lose out, tied to the house.
, how are you?
You look a little pale today.
Someone must worry for you. Do take care.
Perhaps I'll go out again later for a change.
I've had enough of being shut up at home.
Good evening, fair lady.
Oh, good evening. And who might you be?
Pardon me. My name is
You seemed so lonely as you walked.
And, like me, you are not English,
note: Followed by #5216 'it seems.' on the next line.

en: Yes, I was born and raised in France.
My name is Bridget.
Do I look lonely?
In truth, I am.
I have nothing to do.
I can't even look after my own baby.
The nanny takes everything off my hands.
They say a lady doesn't raise her children.
It's absurd.
You do love walking about town, don't you.
Yet you wear such a grave face for it.
Is something the matter?
! How nice to see you.
Where do you go, day after day?
<Just out for a walk>
<I have a matter to look into>
note: Choice after msg 291751; investigation branch -> msg 291784 (#7398-#7400).

en: My, you really do love walking.
That's rare to hear from a man.
I see. You must have your reasons.
Did you make any progress today?
I pray it turns out well for you.
You look well.
I went shopping today, too.
When my child is older, we'll go out together.
For now I must leave it all to the nanny.
It's a little lonely, but it can't be helped.
What brings a gentleman to a ladies' hat shop?
Forgive the intrusion, fair lady.
I'm ashamed to say I have lost my way.
I shall leave at once.
Oh, please... don't trouble yourself.
I am Bridget.
I trust we'll meet again. Good day.
Oh, you are
note: Followed by #152 '...' then a line break: 'Oh, you are... / {NAME}, if I recall.'

en: , if I recall.
Hee hee. A hat for your wife, perhaps?
And you, madam? Out shopping?
Well, yes
Not that I really wish to buy anything.
There's simply nothing for me to do at home.
It just passes the time.
Every day is so dull
I'd almost rather work with the servants.
My, you've come to this shop again?
Are you so very fond of hats?
Hee hee, I'm only joking.
The servants do the housework and childcare,
so I simply sit at home.
My, what a surprise
You've come again. What a curious man.
If only my husband were as amusing
as you.
As for my husband, he's away on business
overseas at present.
So I have even less to do.
Perhaps I should find another pastime.
I must make my own life enjoyable.
It's time I found a new pastime, I think.
Perhaps I'll grow flowers in the garden.
